steps.title: Look point and orbit center
steps.explanation:
After loading static, root.position.x=4 moves the model. The camera is fit to the model but target X starts at 0, so it looks toward the origin. Enter target X=4 and Apply. controls.target is a Vector3, distinct from camera.position. Changing only the center changes view direction and orbit.

Drag horizontally and zoom with the wheel. Orbit once also rotates the camera offset .25rad around target. Compare identical actions at target 0 and 4; record target coordinates and model location. controls.update() applies manual camera/target changes.
steps.solutionExplanation: target uses world coordinates. A model local origin need not be the world origin. Failing to update after a target change can cause an abrupt turn on the next input.
steps.expected: At target X=4, the panels are centered and orbit around that center. frames increases during interaction.
hints: Read camera.position separately from controls.target.
The world model-center X is 4.
Enter 4 for target X, Apply, and drag.
questions: What happens if camera position and target coincide?
Why does world-space target matter?

steps.title: Update through damping
steps.explanation:
Damping starts off. Enable it, Apply, drag the canvas, and release. With enableDamping=true and dampingFactor=.15, each update reduces remaining rotation. Drawing once cannot show that continuation.

frame schedules requestAnimationFrame while controls.update() returns true. A change event wakes new input. insideFrame prevents update-driven change events from double-scheduling. Once movement settles, false ends scheduling. Observe frames continuing briefly after release, then stopping.
steps.solutionExplanation: Enabling damping does not create a loop automatically. Keep calling update through the settling period, then wait for input once stable.
steps.expected: With damping, camera and frames continue briefly after release, then stop. Without it, the view settles immediately after input.
hints: Read frames before and after release.
The update return value controls the next frame.
Enable damping, Apply, drag, then wait for idle.
questions: Why is one update insufficient with damping?
Which flag prevents duplicate scheduling from change and update?

steps.title: Continuous and on-demand rendering
steps.explanation:
Demand rendering starts off, so frames keeps increasing without input. Enable it and Apply. Once the camera settles, frames should stop. Drag or change target and confirm both the count and image resume updating.

invalidate schedules only when raf is absent. frame clears the scheduled marker, updates controls, and draws. It reschedules when demand=false or controls are still moving. Resize also invalidates, so opening a hidden 390 preview updates it. Cleanup cancels the pending frame and controls.dispose() removes control listeners.
steps.solutionExplanation: On-demand rendering reduces unnecessary render calls in a static scene. An ongoing animation must keep scheduling updates while it changes. frames counts render calls in this example, not GPU time or browser-wide FPS.
steps.expected: Off: count rises while idle. On: it stops after settling and resumes during input and damping.
hints: Do not call extra draw while reading the idle count.
Change demand independently of damping.
Enable demand, Apply, and record idle → drag → idle.
questions: Is stopped frames a success if input also fails?
Why is this count not GPU performance?

lessons.introduction: Connect time, models, and update flow from 01, 14, and 16 to clip playback. A clip stores timed values, an action stores playback state, and a mixer evaluates actions for one model. animated moves Left over one second; static has no clips. Record playback state, time in seconds, and actual X together.

steps.title: Clip list and clipless models
steps.explanation:
The starter loads static, with an empty clips array. Successful parsing does not imply animation. Read ready and No clips. Playback buttons are disabled, while model/file and recovery controls remain available. Load animated or change the final sample('static') to sample('animated').

Read names and duration from the loader result animations array. new THREE.AnimationMixer(root) targets this model; mixer.clipAction(clips[0]) returns an action, and action.play() schedules it for evaluation. animated has SlideLeft with duration=1 second. Repeat static → animated → static and check that previous playback does not remain active.
steps.solutionExplanation: Do not use clips[0] unconditionally when no clip exists. Stop all actions and uncacheRoot before replacing the model, then make a mixer for the new root. Geometry/material disposal is separate from clearing mixer caches.
steps.expected: static gives ready, clips=[], and disabled playback with other UI live. animated shows SlideLeft:1s and a moving Left panel.
hints: status and clips.length are different facts.
Select animated from built-in models.
Start with sample('animated') and read SlideLeft duration.
questions: Should a valid model without clips be treated as a load error?
Why clear the previous mixer root when switching models?

steps.title: Convert milliseconds to seconds
steps.explanation:
Animation timestamps use milliseconds; AnimationMixer.update(delta) expects seconds. seconds=false passes now-last directly and advances mixer time 1000× too fast. Set seconds=true and read actual delta such as .016s together with mixer time. A 60Hz rate is not guaranteed, so do not hard-code delta=.016.

Play after pause resets last=0 so waiting time is not added in one step. Compare mixer.time growth over about one real second. Left loops from X=-1.1 to -.1, so X alone cannot reveal total elapsed time. Compare at speed 1, then use 2 and check roughly twice the mixer-time growth over equal wall time.
steps.solutionExplanation: Converting delta to seconds makes playback depend on elapsed time rather than frame count. timeScale scales that seconds delta. Do not apply speed twice by multiplying both delta and timeScale.
steps.expected: false advances mixer roughly 1000× real time. At true and speed=1, about one real second adds about one mixer second.
hints: Distinguish timestamp from its difference to the prior frame.
(now-last)/1000 is seconds.
Set seconds=true and measure at speed=1.
questions: Why does a delta fixed for 60Hz cause trouble?
Why does looping X differ from mixer.time?

steps.title: Action play, pause, stop, and speed
steps.explanation:
The starter prepares an action but playing=false leaves time unchanged. Click Play and read X and mixer time. Pause preserves the pose using action.paused=true; Play resumes from it. Stop and rewind uses action.stop(), reset(), and mixer.time=0 to restore the start pose.

Enter speed=2 and Apply speed. mixer.timeScale=2 evaluates twice as fast over equal real time. Speed 0 is valid and leaves UI live. Compare stop → play, loading clipless static, and loading animated again. Cleanup separately stops the loop, calls stopAllAction()/uncacheRoot(root), and releases actual model resources.
steps.solutionExplanation: Stop unschedules the action and restores original property values. Pause retains scheduling while holding action time. Do not reuse old actions for a new root after model replacement.
steps.expected: While paused, X and mixer.time stay fixed; Play resumes. Stop gives time=0 and Left X=-1.1. speed=2 runs twice as fast as 1.
hints: Read playing and action.paused together.
Apply after entering a numeric speed.
Compare Play → Pause → Play → Stop and speeds 1/2.
questions: How do pause and stop differ for the pose?
Does clearing the mixer automatically dispose geometry?

lessons.introduction: Continue view and material concepts from 03 and 09 with intersecting transparent planes. Red and blue share center depth but exchange front/back across the image. Change opacity, transparent, depthWrite, and object order separately; record overlap colors at the same view. Object sorting cannot fully solve transparency for intersecting surfaces.

steps.title: opacity and the transparent pass
steps.explanation:
The starter has opacity=.45 but transparent=false, so the planes render opaque. Enable transparent and Apply. opacity=.45 controls the source contribution; blending must be enabled to mix with colors behind it. Compare 0, .45, and 1 at the same overlap.

red rotates Y=.65rad and blue Y=-.65rad; DoubleSide shows their back faces too. Change one input, Apply, and read actual material values alongside the image. Even opacity=0 can write depth with depthWrite=true and hide later surfaces; distinguish that in the next step.
steps.solutionExplanation: opacity alone does not move a material into the transparent pass. Set needsUpdate after changing transparent. MeshBasicMaterial removes lighting differences from this comparison.
steps.expected: With transparent=false, .45 still looks opaque. With true, colors and background blend; opacity 0/1 changes their contribution.
hints: Treat opacity and transparent as separate settings.
Enable transparent before comparing opacity.
Apply transparent=true and opacity=.45.
questions: What should you check first when opacity=.45 still looks opaque?
Does opacity=0 automatically disable depth writes?

steps.title: Compare depthWrite
steps.explanation:
Keep transparent=true and opacity=.45. The starter has depthWrite=true. With intersecting planes, depth already written by part of one plane can block later blending. Disable only depthWrite, Apply, and compare left/right overlaps at the same view.

depthTest stays true. depthWrite=false stops writing this surface depth; it does not disable testing against previously drawn opaque objects. Compare on/off under auto and red-last separately. Reducing missing surfaces does not guarantee correct blending order.
steps.solutionExplanation: Transparent objects generally blend back to front, often benefiting from disabled depth writes. Intersecting surfaces have no single front/back object order, so this setting cannot fully solve them.
steps.expected: With false, previously blocked color can blend again. Only depthWrite changes; opacity=.45 and transparent=true remain.
hints: Keep view and opacity fixed.
Distinguish depthWrite from depthTest.
Disable depthWrite, Apply, and compare left and right.
questions: How does not writing depth differ from not testing it?
Why can blending order remain wrong with depthWrite=false?

steps.title: Limits of object sorting
steps.explanation:
With transparent=true and depthWrite=false, apply auto → red-last → blue-last separately. renderOrder=1 draws an object later within this transparent list. Equal-depth centers still force auto sorting to put one whole object first.

At the same front view, changing order changes overlap color. Drawing red last mixes its contribution later on both sides even though actual front/back surfaces swap at the center. Compare right and left views too. renderOrder may improve one region while worsening another or another view. Record view, order, and incorrect regions without calling this a complete solution.
steps.solutionExplanation: Source-over color blending depends on order. Ordinary Three.js sorting works per object without automatically splitting intersecting triangles. Surface splitting or other transparency techniques are beyond this example; the exercise reproduces the limitation.
steps.expected: red-last and blue-last produce different overlap colors at the same pixels. Neither order correctly resolves both sides from every view.
hints: First change only order at the front view.
Equal center depth does not mean equal surface depth on each side.
Apply auto/red-last/blue-last, then compare views.
questions: Why can center-based object sorting not resolve intersecting triangles?
Why is an attractive single view insufficient to claim a general solution?

lessons.introduction: Continue transforms, geometry, and sharing from 04, 05, and 07. A 25-column by 20-row grid contains 500 cubes sharing geometry and material. Apply Mesh then InstancedMesh. Keep camera, coordinates, and count fixed; record calls, triangles, and layout.

steps.title: Individual Mesh objects
steps.explanation: Continue transforms, geometry, and sharing from 04, 05, and 07. A 25-column by 20-row grid contains 500 cubes sharing geometry and material. Apply Mesh then InstancedMesh. Keep camera, coordinates, and count fixed; record calls, triangles, and layout.
steps.solutionExplanation: Shared references alone do not merge calls. InstancedMesh draws one geometry with multiple matrices.
steps.expected: Mesh calls=500, InstancedMesh calls=1; both have triangles=6000.
hints: Check that both representations read the same positions array.
Keep geometry, material, and camera fixed; change only representation.
At 500 cubes compare calls=500 and 1 while triangles stay 6000.
questions: Which comparison condition should you check if layout changes?

steps.title: CPU matrices and GPU uploads
steps.explanation: The starter uses InstancedMesh with upload unchecked. Apply X shift=0.8. CPU X[0] becomes -1.6 but the image stays unchanged. Check upload and Apply again. Initial matrices are uploaded once before the first render.
steps.solutionExplanation: setMatrixAt writes the CPU array. Set needsUpdate=true once after the loop to upload it.
steps.expected: With upload off, version and image remain unchanged. With upload on, version increases and all 500 cubes move.
hints: Read CPU X[0] separately from the image.
Check whether instanceMatrix.version increases after setMatrixAt.
Check upload and Apply X=0.8 again.
questions: What is missing when CPU and image positions differ?

steps.title: Statistics under equal conditions
steps.explanation: The starter count is 100. Set 500 and compare Mesh with InstancedMesh. 100 cubes give triangles=1200; 500 give 6000. Explain why fewer calls do not guarantee improved FPS. This scene has one pass per frame.
steps.solutionExplanation: renderer.info.render reports actual counts. This single pass uses default autoReset; counts are neither timing nor GPU utilization.
steps.expected: At 500 cubes, calls change 500→1 while triangles remain 6000→6000.
hints: First check whether count is 100 or 500.
Each cube contains 12 triangles.
Fix count at 500 and record actual statistics for Mesh and InstancedMesh separately.
questions: Which changes reduce calls and triangles respectively?

lessons.introduction: Continue raycasting and instancing from 13 and 19. Pointer selection starts disabled. Enable it and click the center cube. All three share one object, but left/center/right instanceId values are 0/1/2. NDC uses the actual canvas rectangle; check selection after margins and resize.

steps.title: Object and instanceId
steps.explanation: Continue raycasting and instancing from 13 and 19. Pointer selection starts disabled. Enable it and click the center cube. All three share one object, but left/center/right instanceId values are 0/1/2. NDC uses the actual canvas rectangle; check selection after margins and resize.
steps.solutionExplanation: Keeping only intersection.object loses the instance identity. Keep intersection.instanceId too.
steps.expected: Clicking center yields instanceId=1; empty space yields null.
hints: Enable pointer selection if unchecked.
Distinguish object from instanceId in the intersection.
Click the center cube and verify instanceId=1.
questions: Which value distinguishes cubes sharing the same object?

steps.title: Upload selected matrix and color
steps.explanation: Select center and Apply X=4. Upload starts off, changing only CPU matrix/color data. Enable upload and Apply again to see movement and red color. Instances 0 and 2 must stay unchanged. Set matrix and color needsUpdate separately.
steps.solutionExplanation: setMatrixAt and setColorAt write different buffers. Uploading only position can leave the old color.
steps.expected: Uploading both buffers turns only instance 1 into a red cube at X=4.
hints: Select the center cube before moving it.
Matrix and color buffers have separate upload flags.
Enable upload and Apply X=4 to move only the selected cube.
questions: Does uploading the matrix also upload color?

steps.title: Reselect using refreshed bounds
steps.explanation: Bounds recomputation starts off. Select center, Apply X=4, then click the red cube at its new position. The old sphere rejects the ray first, giving null. Enable recomputation, reset, and repeat selection, Apply, and reselect.
steps.solutionExplanation: Uploading matrices and refreshing CPU bounds are separate. Call computeBoundingBox and computeBoundingSphere after setMatrixAt.
steps.expected: The new position gives null with stale bounds and instanceId=1 after refresh. Sphere center and radius change too.
hints: Check whether selection misses the visible new position.
Raycast tests the aggregate boundingSphere before individual instances.
Enable bounds recomputation, reset, select center, Apply X=4, then select the new position.
questions: Why can raycast miss a visible cube?

lessons.introduction: Continue cameras, vertices, and bounds from 03, 05, and 20. Actual vertices are at X=8 but the starter sphere stays at the origin. The camera targets X=8, leaving an empty image and calls=0. Enable recomputation and Apply; compare sphere center and image.

steps.title: Vertices and stale bounds
steps.explanation: Continue cameras, vertices, and bounds from 03, 05, and 20. Actual vertices are at X=8 but the starter sphere stays at the origin. The camera targets X=8, leaving an empty image and calls=0. Enable recomputation and Apply; compare sphere center and image.
steps.solutionExplanation: Position attributes and boundingSphere are separate data. Recompute existing bounds after vertex edits.
steps.expected: After recomputation, center.x=8 and the cube reappears.
hints: Compare vertex X=8 with sphere center.x.
The camera already targets X=8; keep it fixed.
Enable bounds recomputation and Apply to obtain center.x=8 and restore drawing.
questions: Why can calls be zero when vertices are inside the view?

steps.title: Culling bypass and actual repair
steps.explanation: The starter has frustumCulled=false, so the cube remains visible despite stale bounds. Disable recomputation and enable culling to reproduce disappearance. Then enable recomputation and Apply to restore it while keeping culling. Distinguish bypassing culling from correcting bounds.
steps.solutionExplanation: Use frustumCulled=false for diagnosis. This exercise fixes the bounds to match vertex positions.
steps.expected: Stale bounds with culling on give an empty image; off shows the cube. Fresh bounds with culling on show it too.
hints: Toggle culling while keeping stale bounds.
Culling off bypasses the test without correcting bounds.
Keep culling on and Apply bounds recomputation to restore the cube.
questions: How do bypassing culling and fixing bounds differ in cost?

steps.title: Distance and actual triangle counts
steps.explanation: Select LOD and Apply distances 4 then 12. Model center and target stay at X=8; only camera Z changes. At distance 8, an icosahedron with detail=2 switches to detail=0. Record silhouette edges, LOD index, and triangles.
steps.solutionExplanation: IcosahedronGeometry detail=2 divides each face into 9 triangles, totaling 180. addLevel distance is measured from world model position to the camera.
steps.expected: Distance 4 gives level=0 and triangles=180; distance 12 gives level=1 and triangles=20.
hints: Select the LOD experiment.
Model and target remain X=8; change only distance from 4 to 12.
Compare level and actual triangles=180/20 across threshold 8.
questions: Which camera/model conditions should accompany quality and cost observations?

lessons.introduction: Continue renderer, cameras, and textures from 02, 03, and 10. Target updates start disabled. Enable and Apply to populate the minimap. Apply X=1.5, disable updates, then Apply X=-1.5. The main view moves while the minimap keeps the old position. Reenable updates to synchronize.

steps.title: Draw into a texture
steps.explanation: Continue renderer, cameras, and textures from 02, 03, and 10. Target updates start disabled. Enable and Apply to populate the minimap. Apply X=1.5, disable updates, then Apply X=-1.5. The main view moves while the minimap keeps the old position. Reenable updates to synchronize.
steps.solutionExplanation: setRenderTarget(target) changes the destination of subsequent renders. A material using its texture displays the result in another pass.
steps.expected: With updates on both views reflect the same X; off freezes only the minimap.
hints: If the map is empty, check Update target.
Change X with updates off and compare main and map.
Reenable updates and Apply to refresh target.texture.
questions: Which pass stopped when only the main view moves?

steps.title: Two cameras and a display pass
steps.explanation: Enable Show minimap and Apply. Main camera at (5,5,7) and mini camera at (0,8,0) target the origin. miniCamera.up=(0,0,-1) fixes map orientation. Compare X=-1.5 then 1.5 to observe the same cube from two views. Blue stays at (1.5,0,-1.5), so red does not overlap it at the assigned X values.
steps.solutionExplanation: An orthographic camera renders the overlay plane in a separate scene. Do not sample a target texture while rendering into that same target.
steps.expected: Main view shows cube sides; the map shows top faces. A 128×128 target is displayed at bottom right.
hints: Check Show minimap.
The mini camera looks down from Y=8 with up along -Z.
Apply X=-1.5 and 1.5 to compare side and top views of the same cube.
questions: What would remain identical if both views used the same camera?

steps.title: Restore target, viewport, and scissor
steps.explanation: Restoration starts disabled, leaving the main canvas empty or stale. Enable it and Apply. The helper saves target, active face, mipmap level, viewport, scissor, and scissorTest on entry and restores them in finally. Restoring to a hardcoded null can break a caller already using another target.
steps.solutionExplanation: The target owns its texture, so dispose the target once without separately disposing the shared map. Accumulate all frame passes with autoReset=false, then restore the default.
steps.expected: With restoration on, target=screen and both views update again. State before and after the helper matches.
hints: Read whether output target is screen or texture.
setRenderTarget(null) alone cannot restore all caller state.
Restore saved target, face, mip, viewport, scissor, and test in finally.
questions: How should you restore a caller whose previous target was not null?

lessons.introduction: Press remove. The left cube disappears while geometry and material disposal counts remain 0. Reattach renders the same references. Removal only breaks the parent connection.

steps.title: Detach and GPU resources
steps.explanation: Press remove. The left cube disappears while geometry and material disposal counts remain 0. Reattach renders the same references. Removal only breaks the parent connection.
steps.solutionExplanation: After remove: children=1, disposed=0; reattach restores children=2. Observe a.parent separately from dispose events.
steps.expected: After remove: children=1, disposed=0; reattach restores children=2.
hints: Observe a.parent separately from dispose events.
questions: Why can the detached object be reused?

steps.title: Release the last user
steps.explanation: Press release A then release B. With disposal disabled initially, dropping the last reference emits no GPU disposal event. Enable disposal and press collect to dispose geometry and material once each.
steps.solutionExplanation: First release: ref=1, disposed=0. Collect after the final release: ref=0, disposed=2. Collect only entries whose ref count is 0.
steps.expected: First release: ref=1, disposed=0. Collect after the final release: ref=0, disposed=2.
hints: Collect only entries whose ref count is 0.
questions: Does remove alone clean GPU resources?

steps.title: Shared ownership and repeated cleanup
steps.explanation: Enable the shared ledger. A and B use the same geometry and material, giving ref=2. Inspect B after release A, then release B. Press cycle 3 times: each creates and disposes one geometry and one material. Calling full cleanup twice must not dispose twice.
steps.solutionExplanation: B survives release A; after 3 cycles, created minus disposed equals live resources. The starter without the ledger retains ref=2 after A is removed.
steps.expected: B survives release A; after 3 cycles, created minus disposed equals live resources.
hints: The starter without the ledger retains ref=2 after A is removed.
questions: What fails if each mesh disposes its shared resources immediately?

lessons.introduction: Enable generation protection. Press slow A then fast B. A waits 300ms after real textured GLB parsing; B waits 20ms after animated parsing. The unprotected starter lets A overwrite the scene. Repeat with protection and confirm B remains.

steps.title: Request and completion order
steps.explanation: Enable generation protection. Press slow A then fast B. A waits 300ms after real textured GLB parsing; B waits 20ms after animated parsing. The unprotected starter lets A overwrite the scene. Repeat with protection and confirm B remains.
steps.solutionExplanation: Completion log is B then A; current model remains B. Compare the request token with the current generation.
steps.expected: Completion log is B then A; current model remains B.
hints: Compare the request token with the current generation.
questions: Does starting first guarantee permission to apply?

steps.title: Own and release stale parse results
steps.explanation: Enable stale cleanup and reverse completion order. Parsed textured A owns real geometry, material, texture and ImageBitmap resources. Release late A without attaching it. Inspect bitmap close and disposal counts.
steps.solutionExplanation: B remains; A geometry, material, texture and bitmap are released. Release the ownership ledger before returning.
steps.expected: B remains; A geometry, material, texture and bitmap are released.
hints: Release the ownership ledger before returning.
questions: Is preserving the UI sufficient stale handling?

steps.title: Keep the current scene after failure
steps.explanation: Press invalid GLB and confirm the current model and object list remain. Recover sample loads animated again. Continue using the same controls after failure. Local files pass through the same validation and parseAsync.
steps.solutionExplanation: The current model remains visible in error; recovery returns to ready. Do not clear root before a load succeeds.
steps.expected: The current model remains visible in error; recovery returns to ready.
hints: Do not clear root before a load succeeds.
questions: May an older failure change the latest successful state?

lessons.introduction: Enable list wiring and apply. Tab to Objects and select Right with ArrowDown. The list change updates selection and text together. The canvas image alone does not name the selection.

steps.title: Object list outside canvas
steps.explanation: Enable list wiring and apply. Tab to Objects and select Right with ArrowDown. The list change updates selection and text together. The canvas image alone does not name the selection.
steps.solutionExplanation: Selection status names Right and index 1. Check the label, select change handler and status text.
steps.expected: Selection status names Right and index 1.
hints: Check the label, select change handler and status text.
questions: How is the 3D object name exposed to assistive technology?

steps.title: Keyboard camera controls
steps.explanation: Enable keyboard camera controls and apply. Tab to camera buttons and use Enter for right, zoom in and frame selected. Read the image and camera coordinates. Controls are native buttons.
steps.solutionExplanation: Right increases camera.x by 1; zoom in reduces z by 1. Avoid hiding every command behind canvas keydown.
steps.expected: Right increases camera.x by 1; zoom in reduces z by 1.
hints: Avoid hiding every command behind canvas keydown.
questions: How does a keyboard user locate focus?

steps.title: Error announcements and recovery focus
steps.explanation: Enable status announcements and apply. Use only Tab and Enter to trigger failure and recovery. The list and camera controls remain after failure; role=status announces the error and recovery guidance. Recovery focuses the list.
steps.solutionExplanation: Failure is announced as text; recovery focuses Objects. aria-live needs changed text to announce.
steps.expected: Failure is announced as text; recovery focuses Objects.
hints: aria-live needs changed text to announce.
questions: What is lost when an error is conveyed only by color?

lessons.introduction: Enable frame totals and apply. In one pass two cubes give calls=2 and triangles=24. Two measurements should agree. Reset once at the start of each logical frame.

steps.title: Draw calls in one pass
steps.explanation: Enable frame totals and apply. In one pass two cubes give calls=2 and triangles=24. Two measurements should agree. Reset once at the start of each logical frame.
steps.solutionExplanation: At fixed size, camera and count: calls=2, triangles=24. Interpret info.render only with its accumulation interval.
steps.expected: At fixed size, camera and count: calls=2, triangles=24.
hints: Interpret info.render only with its accumulation interval.
questions: What happens if frames accumulate without reset?

steps.title: Whole-frame totals across passes
steps.explanation: The multi-pass starter uses autoReset=true and shows only the last pass calls=2. Enable frame totals and apply. Mini and main cameras each draw both cubes.
steps.solutionExplanation: Frame totals are calls=4 and triangles=48. Do not reset before every render.
steps.expected: Frame totals are calls=4 and triangles=48.
hints: Do not reset before every render.
questions: Which comparison fails if the last pass is mistaken for the whole frame?

steps.title: Measure under fixed conditions
steps.explanation: Measure passes 1 then 2. Keep count=2, DPR=1, CSS size up to 480×280 and the same camera. CPU ms is elapsed performance.now call time, not exact GPU duration or an improvement rate.
steps.solutionExplanation: Doubling passes doubles this scene calls and triangles; CPU ms may vary between runs. Record JIT, uploads, SwiftShader and canvas size as conditions.
steps.expected: Doubling passes doubles this scene calls and triangles; CPU ms may vary between runs.
hints: Record JIT, uploads, SwiftShader and canvas size as conditions.
questions: Does reducing triangles always preserve visual quality?

lessons.introduction: Change sample static to animated and load. Scene, list and mixer change together only after success. Files exist only during this execution.

steps.title: Load a model into the inspector
steps.explanation: Change sample static to animated and load. Scene, list and mixer change together only after success. Files exist only during this execution.
steps.solutionExplanation: Animated has Left and Right plus one SlideLeft clip. Finish parsing before replacing the owned scene.
steps.expected: Animated has Left and Right plus one SlideLeft clip.
hints: Finish parsing before replacing the owned scene.
questions: What must survive a fallible load?

steps.title: Connect selection and camera
steps.explanation: Select Right and press frame selected. Enable framing and apply because it starts disabled. Update camera position and direction from the Box3 center and size.
steps.solutionExplanation: Target becomes the selected object center and it appears at screen center. Position alone may leave the camera facing the old origin.
steps.expected: Target becomes the selected object center and it appears at screen center.
hints: Position alone may leave the camera facing the old origin.
questions: How is selection connected to the camera target?

steps.title: Control the loaded clip
steps.explanation: Load animated and press play. Change the starter speed 0 to 1 and apply. Left X changes with time. Inspect pause, then stop to rewind.
steps.solutionExplanation: At speed=1 Left moves; pause keeps time and stop restores the initial position. Pass seconds to mixer.update.
steps.expected: At speed=1 Left moves; pause keeps time and stop restores the initial position.
hints: Pass seconds to mixer.update.
questions: Why uncache the mixer before model replacement?

steps.title: Connect motion to the minimap
steps.explanation: Enable the minimap and apply. Render the same scene to a target with a separate camera, then display it at bottom right. Change selection and animation and inspect both views.
steps.solutionExplanation: Minimap on adds target and display passes to frame totals. Restore target, viewport and scissor in finally.
steps.expected: Minimap on adds target and display passes to frame totals.
hints: Restore target, viewport and scissor in finally.
questions: Which update do you inspect when the minimap stops?

steps.title: Recover the inspector
steps.explanation: Trigger invalid GLB, slow A then fast B and recover sample. List, selection, camera, playback and minimap controls survive failure and stale results. After recovery use keyboard selection, framing and playback again.
steps.solutionExplanation: Failure preserves the current scene; late A is released after B. Rebuild the list only on successful commit.
steps.expected: Failure preserves the current scene; late A is released after B.
hints: Rebuild the list only on successful commit.
questions: Which features must continue working together after failure?

lessons.introduction: Measure to create a baseline. Keep count=8, segments=16 and passes=1. Read camera, buffer, DPR, calls, triangles and CPU ms. No initial record means no measurement yet.

steps.title: Capture a real comparison baseline
steps.explanation: Measure to create a baseline. Keep count=8, segments=16 and passes=1. Read camera, buffer, DPR, calls, triangles and CPU ms. No initial record means no measurement yet.
steps.solutionExplanation: The first measurement and conditions are appended to the record. Capture the actual frame when Measure is pressed.
steps.expected: The first measurement and conditions are appended to the record.
hints: Capture the actual frame when Measure is pressed.
questions: Can a number without conditions be compared later?

steps.title: Compare quality and cost
steps.explanation: Measure segments 16 then change to 8 and measure again. Fix count, passes and camera. Compare sphere silhouettes alongside triangles. The starter and solution shapes illustrate quality cost.
steps.solutionExplanation: At 8, triangles decrease and silhouettes change. No invented improvement rate is calculated. Change geometry within the same layout.
steps.expected: At 8, triangles decrease and silhouettes change. No invented improvement rate is calculated.
hints: Change geometry within the same layout.
questions: Does a lower triangle count prove preserved quality?

steps.title: Ledger for repeated creation and release
steps.explanation: Press cycle 3 times. Each releases current resources and rebuilds under the same conditions. Created minus disposed is 1 for geometry and material each. After cleanup record whether the difference is 0.
steps.solutionExplanation: After 3 cycles each disposed count increases by 3; cleanup makes it equal created. renderer.info.memory includes internal caches, so do not demand zero.
steps.expected: After 3 cycles each disposed count increases by 3; cleanup makes it equal created.
hints: renderer.info.memory includes internal caches, so do not demand zero.
questions: How does the ownership ledger differ from renderer.info.memory?

steps.title: Transfer observations into existing notes
steps.explanation: Create 16 versus 8 segment measurements and 3 cycle results. Press Select report and copy with Ctrl+C, then paste into the site Notes tab. Add conditions, actual values, visual differences, cleanup results and measurement limits in your own words; use existing save and backup.
steps.solutionExplanation: The report contains actual measurements and release counts and is preserved in site notes. The example iframe does not directly access parent storage.
steps.expected: The report contains actual measurements and release counts and is preserved in site notes.
hints: The example iframe does not directly access parent storage.
questions: Why is CPU call time not exact GPU execution time?

apis.description: Constructor for a scene root. Scene inherits Object3D and connects children with add. Its background member defaults to null.
apis.result: Returns a new Scene. Construction alone does not draw to a canvas.
cautions: Scene is not an HTML element.

apis.description: Constructor for a color object. This course uses CSS hex strings only.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A CSS hex color string, such as '#edf2f7'.

apis.result: Returns a new Color.
cautions: Color spaces and linear RGB calculations are later topics.

apis.description: Constructor for a renderer that draws WebGL2 scenes to a canvas. domElement refers to its actual output canvas.

parameters.name: canvas
parameters.description: The canvas selected from HTML. Omitting it creates a new canvas.

apis.result: Returns a renderer. domElement is a canvas reference, not a method.
cautions: WebGL2 support is required. Pass your existing canvas to use it.
apis.example:
const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ canvas, antialias: true });
const actualCanvas = renderer.domElement;

apis.description: Instance method that sets renderer logical size and viewport. It also resizes the canvas buffer using DPR.

parameters.name: updateStyle
parameters.description: When true, also changes canvas inline CSS width and height.

apis.result: No return value. The buffer becomes floor(width*DPR) × floor(height*DPR).
cautions: Use false when CSS manages display size. Do not pass dimensions already multiplied by DPR.

apis.description: Instance method that draws the scene through a camera onto the current canvas.

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: The camera defining position, direction, and projection.

apis.result: No return value. Updates the current image.
cautions: Changing object properties does not automatically call this method.

apis.description: Constructor for a perspective camera, where distant objects appear smaller. Arguments are positional.

parameters.name: fov
parameters.description: Vertical field of view in degrees.

parameters.name: near
parameters.description: Depth of the near plane in front of the camera.

apis.result: Returns a new PerspectiveCamera.
cautions: Set near>0 and far>near. fov uses degrees rather than the radians used by rotation.
Call updateProjectionMatrix after changing fov/aspect/near/far/zoom.
apis.example: const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(50, w / h, .1, 50);

apis.description: Constructor for a box centered at the origin, with edges parallel to local X/Y/Z.
apis.result: Returns a new BoxGeometry.
cautions: Segment arguments are omitted here and each defaults to 1. Editing parameters.width does not rebuild vertices.

apis.description: Constructor for a surface appearance unaffected by lights.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: The examples use CSS hex strings.

apis.result: Returns a new material.
cautions: If this material is invisible, check Scene connection, camera, and render before adding lights.

apis.description: Constructor for a scene object combining geometry and material.
apis.result: Returns a new Mesh without adding it to Scene.
cautions: This course supplies both arguments rather than relying on omitted defaults.
apis.example:
const cube = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
scene.add(cube);

apis.description: position is a Vector3 member holding a position relative to the parent. position.set is a Vector3 method that changes its components.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Position along the parent X axis.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Position along the parent Y axis.

parameters.name: z
parameters.description: Position along the parent Z axis.

apis.result: position initially is (0, 0, 0). set mutates it and returns the same Vector3.
cautions: Change x/y/z or use set; do not replace position with an array.

apis.description: Method that points a camera toward a world-space target.

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: Target world X. An overload accepts a single Vector3.

apis.result: No return value. Changes camera rotation without moving its position.
cautions: Non-uniformly scaled parents are unsupported. With controls, avoid having lookAt and controls.update overwrite orientation each frame.

apis.description: Method that connects other Object3D instances as children.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: Children to connect. Multiple arguments are accepted.

apis.result: Returns the parent itself. Children are removed from their previous parents.
cautions: An object has one parent. Its local transform is retained, but its world position is not guaranteed to stay the same.

apis.description: Euler member holding an Object3D local rotation. x/y/z are angles in radians.
apis.result: Initial angles are (0, 0, 0), with default order XYZ. Assigning components mutates the object.
cautions: Math.PI / 2 is 90°. Do not confuse radians with camera.fov degrees.
A child rotation.y is not always a rotation about world Y.

apis.description: Method that registers or stops a callback for each frame.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: The first callback argument in this non-XR example is timestamp timeMs. null stops the loop.

apis.result: No return value. The registered callback runs repeatedly.
cautions: The timestamp is in ms; elapsed seconds are (timeMs-start)/1000.
After changing object values inside the callback, also call render.

apis.description: Constructor for an Object3D node that groups child transforms. It has no shape of its own.
apis.result: Returns a new Group. position/rotation/add follow Object3D contracts.
cautions: Adding a Group does not create visible geometry.

apis.description: Constructor for an object with x/y/z components, used here to store position results.
apis.result: Returns a new Vector3.
cautions: The Vector3 type does not determine whether a value is local or world-space; its use does.

apis.description: Method that reads world position including current parent transforms.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: The destination object for the result; it is required.

apis.result: Mutates and returns target without changing object.position.
cautions: In 0.186.1, the method updates the required parent world matrices internally. No manual matrix multiplication is needed.

apis.description: Method that applies changed fov/aspect/near/far/zoom values to the projection matrix. Orthographic cameras expose the same method.
apis.result: No return value. The next render uses the updated projection.
cautions: Property assignment does not call this automatically.
Distinguish camera movement from changes to projection values.

apis.description: DOM members for display and buffer dimensions. clientWidth/clientHeight use CSS px; canvas.width/height use buffer px. The same Element clientWidth/clientHeight contract applies to canvas.
apis.result: Property reads yield dimension numbers. Client dimensions are integers and include padding but exclude borders. The corresponding scrollbar is also excluded.
cautions: These are Web APIs, not Three.js APIs. packageVersion records the lesson Three.js version.
The example stage has no padding/border. Do not mix direct canvas buffer assignments with renderer size management.
Display-size sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/clientWidth and https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/clientHeight

apis.description: Web API that reports element size changes through a callback, including stage changes without window resizing.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.description: Function called for size changes. The generic snippet below passes resizeScene; unit 01 passes draw.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Element observed with observe(target). The snippet uses stage; unit 01 observes canvas.

apis.result: The constructor returns an observer. observe and disconnect return no value. disconnect stops observation.
cautions: This is not a Three.js API. packageVersion records the lesson Three.js version.
Return before division if w or h is 0. An observer does not replace render.

apis.description: Method that sets buffer pixels per CSS pixel. getPixelRatio() takes no arguments and returns the currently configured ratio as a number.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The experiment explicitly uses 1 or 2. The initial renderer ratio is 1.

apis.result: No return value. Resizes the buffer using the current logical size.
cautions: It does not automatically read devicePixelRatio.
A ratio of 2 affects both axes, giving 4 times as many pixels, not necessarily 4 times the processing time.

apis.description: Constructor for an orthographic camera, where size does not change with depth. Bounds use camera-space units.
apis.result: Returns a new OrthographicCamera. zoom defaults to 1.
cautions: Do not resize by setting an aspect property. Keep halfHeight and update left/right=±halfHeight*aspect.
Call updateProjectionMatrix after changing bounds or zoom.
apis.example:
const halfHeight = 3;
const ortho = new THREE.OrthographicCamera(-halfHeight * aspect, halfHeight * aspect, halfHeight, -halfHeight, .1, 30);

apis.description: Numeric projection members: fov in degrees, aspect as width/height, near/far as depth, and zoom as magnification.
apis.result: PerspectiveCamera defaults are fov=50, aspect=1, near=.1, far=2000, zoom=1. Projection must be updated after assignment.
cautions: near/far are planes at camera-space depths, not spheres of distance from the origin.
Orthographic cameras have no fov; zoom and left/right/top/bottom set their range. Use positive zoom in the experiments.

apis.description: Addon constructor for moving a camera around a target. It requires a separate import.

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: The perspective or orthographic camera to control.

apis.result: Returns new controls, with target initially (0, 0, 0).
cautions: Left drag orbits the camera; the wheel changes perspective distance or orthographic zoom.
On camera replacement, dispose old controls and create controls for the new camera.
apis.example:
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
const controls = new OrbitControls(camera, canvas);

apis.description: target is a world-space Vector3; enabled permits input interaction; enableDamping enables inertia.
apis.result: Defaults are target=(0, 0, 0), enabled=true, enableDamping=false. Assignment changes the same controls instance.
cautions: Call update after target.set and every frame when damping is enabled.
Even with enabled=false, an explicit update can perform calculations. Control those calls in comparison mode.

apis.description: Instance method that applies camera and target state.

parameters.name: deltaTime
parameters.description: Optional elapsed time in seconds. These examples omit it because autoRotate is not used.

apis.result: Returns a boolean indicating change. May update camera position, orientation, or zoom.
cautions: Call after manual camera/target changes.
Avoid overwriting orientation with lookAt each frame.

apis.description: Method that releases event connections owned by controls.
apis.result: No return value. Call when finished with the old controls.
cautions: It does not release geometry/material GPU resources.

apis.description: Constructor and update method for lines visualizing a camera frustum.

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: The subjectCamera whose frustum is visualized.

apis.result: The constructor returns a helper; update has no return value and refreshes lines after projection changes.
cautions: Place helper directly under scene. Add subjectCamera to scene so its world transform updates while rendering from overview.
Observe a camera frustum from a separate overviewCamera.

apis.description: Boolean member controlling scene-object visibility, initially true.
apis.result: Assignment changes visibility without deleting the object.
cautions: helper.visible=false hides helper lines without deleting subjectCamera.

apis.description: Constructor for lines showing local positive X/Y/Z axes.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Length of each axis line in scene units.

apis.result: Returns a new helper. X=red, Y=green, Z=blue.
cautions: Under scene it shows world axes; under pivot it follows pivot transforms. Read text labels as well as colors.

apis.description: String member setting Euler intrinsic local-axis rotation order. The default is XYZ.
apis.result: The same x/y/z values can produce different orientations with a different order.
cautions: Do not describe this as world X followed by world Y.
This supplementary experiment does not preserve an old world orientation or implement quaternion conversion.

apis.description: Attach a vertex attribute by name. count is array length divided by itemSize.
apis.result: setAttribute returns the geometry.
cautions: Positions use three components per vertex.

apis.description: Specify three vertex indices per triangle. null uses consecutive vertices.
apis.result: Returns the geometry.
cautions: Out-of-range indices are not repaired automatically. Validate first.

apis.description: Modify a CPU component with setY, then set needsUpdate=true to request GPU upload.

parameters.name: index, y
parameters.description: Vertex index and new y component

apis.result: setY returns the attribute. Setting needsUpdate increments version.
cautions: Recompute bounds after position edits. Do not inspect a needsUpdate getter as confirmation.

apis.description: Calculate normals from faces; indexed geometry accumulates adjacent-face contributions at shared vertices and normalizes them.
apis.result: Updates the normal attribute without returning a value.
cautions: Does not merge duplicate vertices or change winding.

apis.description: Use face normals when true and interpolate vertex normals when false.
apis.result: Changes the material shading mode.
cautions: After compilation, changing it requires material.needsUpdate=true.

apis.description: Copy the Mesh and Object3D transforms while retaining geometry and material references.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Whether to clone child Object3D objects too.

apis.result: Returns a new Mesh.
cautions: Clone resources separately when independent edits are needed.

apis.description: Create a new geometry or material instance.
apis.result: Returns a new resource of the same type.
cautions: Material clones do not independently clone textures. Dispose shared resources once through their owner.

apis.description: Add light equally throughout the scene without direction.
apis.result: A new ambient light; add it to the scene.
cautions: Ambient lights do not cast shadows.

apis.description: Parallel light pointing from position to target world position.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Its default position is the origin.

apis.result: Changing the target changes light direction.
cautions: Add the target to the scene. Rotation does not define direction.

apis.description: Emit light from one point in all directions with distance attenuation.
apis.result: A new point light.
cautions: Distance attenuation still applies when distance=0.

apis.description: Represent a physically based surface using roughness and metalness.
apis.result: A new standard material.
cautions: Without material.envMap, scene.environment uses scene.environmentIntensity. These examples explicitly assign the same envMap to both materials.

apis.description: Capture a scene and prefilter it for roughness-dependent environment reflections.
apis.result: Returns a WebGLRenderTarget containing the texture.
cautions: Dispose the generator and returned target according to their separate lifetimes.

apis.description: Loads an image asynchronously and reports success or failure.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: A data URI or object URL

apis.result: Returns a Texture immediately; onLoad signals image readiness.
cautions: onProgress is unsupported. Texture disposal and object URL revocation are separate.
apis.example: loader.load(url, texture => { material.map=texture; material.needsUpdate=true; }, undefined, showError);

apis.description: Controls UV scale and sampling outside the unit range.

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.description: Horizontal and vertical UV scale; default (1,1)

apis.result: repeat.set(x,y) returns the same Vector2.
cautions: repeat alone does not enable repetition. Set needsUpdate after changing wrapping.

apis.description: Declares color-image encoding or numeric-data semantics.

parameters.name: colorSpace
parameters.description: SRGBColorSpace for color maps; NoColorSpace for numeric maps

apis.result: Sets the annotation used to interpret GPU texture input.
cautions: roughnessMap uses green. normalMap also encodes directions rather than photographic color.

apis.description: Encodes linear working results for display.
apis.result: Property assignment changes render output encoding.
cautions: Do not repair incorrect texture semantics through output settings. Use NoToneMapping for this controlled comparison.

apis.description: Separates depth casters from surfaces that receive shadow comparisons.

parameters.name: castShadow
parameters.description: Whether the object casts; default false

parameters.name: receiveShadow
parameters.description: Whether its surface receives shadows; default false

apis.result: Property assignments have no return value.
cautions: Also enable renderer.shadowMap.enabled and light.castShadow.

apis.description: Defines the light-view region captured by the depth map.
apis.result: Read the camera reference to change its bounds and update projection.
cautions: More map pixels cannot fix missing coverage. Wider bounds increase world units per texel.
apis.example: const c=light.shadow.camera; c.left=c.bottom=-4; c.right=c.top=4; c.updateProjectionMatrix(); helper.update();

apis.description: Sets the depth texture width and height in pixels.
apis.result: Configured dimensions apply when the map is allocated.
cautions: A 16× side increase means 256× texels. Dispose an existing map and set it to null when resizing.

apis.description: Updates the ray origin and direction from NDC and a camera.

parameters.name: coords
parameters.description: Canvas-relative -1–1, with y=1 at the top

parameters.name: camera
parameters.description: The camera used to render the current view

apis.result: Updates the internal ray without a return value.
cautions: Use the current getBoundingClientRect for client coordinates. Distinguish CSS size from buffer pixels.

apis.description: Reads real intersections sorted nearest first.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Whether to inspect descendants; default true, false here

apis.result: Returns Intersection records with object, distance, point, and more.
cautions: Coincident triangle hits are possible. Define your own selection policy for an empty array.

apis.description: Reads world axis-aligned bounds including descendant transforms.
apis.result: setFromObject returns this Box3; isEmpty returns boolean.
cautions: getCenter/getSize write into supplied Vector3 objects. Stop fitting for empty bounds.

apis.description: Uses both FOVs and a bounding sphere for conservative framing.
